prompt_template:
You are an evidence-focused scientific literature analyst. You are given a paper title, journal, and PubMed abstract. Use only the information supplied below.

Produce a concise, scientifically faithful summary that helps a reader quickly understand what the study investigated, how it was approached, and what it found. Keep the assessment general and scientific. Do not judge the paper's relevance to any particular person, project, or research field.

Return exactly one valid JSON object. Do not use Markdown fences or add commentary outside the JSON. Use exactly this schema and no additional fields:
{
  "summary": "A direct overview in 45-85 words, covering the scientific question, approach, main result, and implication where available.",
  "key_findings": [
    "Up to three concise, concrete findings reported in the abstract."
  ],
  "scientific_significance": "One concise sentence describing the broader scientific contribution or what the findings add to scientific understanding, based only on the abstract; otherwise use an empty string."
}

Rules:
- The summary must contain 45-85 words. Count the words before returning the JSON. Do not pad with repetition or unsupported information to reach the target.
- Do not add facts, mechanisms, results, sample sizes, or conclusions that are not supported by the abstract.
- Preserve uncertainty and avoid overstating causality.
- Scientific significance must describe the study's general contribution to scientific understanding, not its relevance to a particular research field, person, or project.
- Do not include a separate limitations section, relevance assessment, personalised assessment, generic caveats, or any fields beyond the three specified above.
- If the abstract is incomplete or unclear, reflect that briefly in the summary rather than adding a separate section.
- Use plain, precise scientific language and avoid repetition.
- Before returning the JSON, silently proofread every field for spelling errors, malformed words, accidental fragments, duplicated phrases, and punctuation mistakes. Correct them without changing the scientific meaning.

article.title: Breaking the Capacity-Reversibility Linear Trade-Off in Li-O2 Batteries via Amorphous Non-Precious High-Entropy Alloy Catalysts.
article.abstract: NA: Lithium-oxygen (Li-O2) batteries suffer from sluggish reaction kinetics and rely on precious metal-based catalysts to facilitate the reaction process. Despite being effective, these costly catalysts would inevitably introduce a critical trade-off between capacity and reversibility, compromising the high energy density advantage of Li-O2 batteries. In this study, we have designed an amorphous non-precious MnFeCoNiCu high-entropy alloy (A-HEA) catalyst via a mild liquid-phase reduction strategy to break the above inherent linear trade-off. The amorphous and porous structure of A-HEA could provide a large electrochemical active surface area, diluting the local current density to promote the solution-mediated discharge pathway. This enables the growth of large-sized Li2O2 to deliver a discharge capacity reaching 10.8 mAh cm-2. Additionally, the multielemental synergistic electron redistribution of A-HEA optimizes the d-band center to strengthen the LiO2 adsorption and weaken the O─O bonding, reducing the overpotential to 0.75 V and extending the battery lifetime by 4-5 times compared to the crystalline counterparts. Importantly, the A-HEA can be produced at a scale of over 100 g and works well in Li-O2 pouch cells with a rate capability up to 400 mA and an energy density of 754 Wh kg-1 (560 Wh kg-1 even at -30°C).

parsed.summary: This study investigates breaking the capacity-reversibility trade-off in Li-O2 batteries using amorphous non-precious MnFeCoNiCu high-entropy alloy (A-HEA) catalysts. The researchers designed A-HEA via liquid-phase reduction to create a porous structure enhancing electrochemical surface area and promoting solution-mediated discharge pathways. The catalyst achieved 10.8 mAh cm-2 capacity with reduced overpotential (0.75 V) and extended cycle life 4-5 times versus crystalline analogs. The material demonstrated scalability and performance in pouch cells at high rates and low temperatures.
key_findings: A-HEA catalyst achieved 10.8 mAh cm-2 discharge capacity
Reduced overpotential to 0.75 V and 4-5x longer cycle life versus crystalline catalysts
Scalable production and high-performance in pouch cells at 400 mA and -30°C
parsed.scientific_significance: This work demonstrates a non-precious catalyst strategy to overcome the fundamental capacity-reversibility trade-off in Li-O2 batteries, enabling higher energy density and longer cycle life without compromising reversibility.

article.title: Immunomodulatory effect of neem leaf glycoprotein (NLGP) through TH1 polarisation and regulatory Treg-associated gene modulation in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
article.abstract: NA: Neem leaf glycoprotein (NLGP), derived from Azadirachta indica, is an immune activator with potential in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) immunotherapy. NSCLC progression supported by regulatory T cells (Tregs) suppress cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) activity and blunt TH1-type responses. We tested whether NLGP can reduce Treg-mediated immunosuppression and shift adaptive immunity towards a tumoricidal TH1-profile. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy controls and NSCLC patients were treated with NLGP and assessed by MTT [3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide], Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), nitric oxide (NO) assays, and qRT-PCR. NLGP treatment produced maximal lymphocyte proliferation, increased CTL-mediated cytotoxicity, and elevated NO release-an effector molecule known to favour TH1 responses. Cytokine profiling showed increased type1-cytokines and upregulation of TH1-specific genes, while TH2-, TH17-, and Treg-associated gene expression declined. Notably, IL10 and Forkhead box P3 (FOXP3) expression dropped after NLGP treatment, indicating suppressed Treg function. These results suggest NLGP promotes antitumor immunity in NSCLC by enhancing CTL activity and TH1 polarisation while restraining Treg-mediated suppression.

parsed.summary: This study investigated NLGP's immunomodulatory effects in NSCLC by assessing its impact on Treg-mediated immunosuppression and TH1 polarization. Using PBMCs from NSCLC patients and healthy controls, NLGP treatment enhanced lymphocyte proliferation, cytotoxic T lymphocyte activity, nitric oxide release, and type 1 cytokine production while reducing TH2, TH17, and Treg-associated gene expression. The results indicate NLGP shifts adaptive immunity toward a tumoricidal TH1 profile by suppressing Treg function.
key_findings: NLGP enhanced lymphocyte proliferation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte activity in NSCLC patient PBMCs
NLGP increased nitric oxide release and type 1 cytokine production while reducing TH2 and TH17 responses
NLGP suppressed Treg-associated genes (IL10 and FOXP3) indicating reduced regulatory T cell function
parsed.scientific_significance: NLGP demonstrates a mechanism for enhancing antitumor immunity in NSCLC by modulating T cell differentiation toward a tumoricidal TH1 response while inhibiting immunosuppressive regulatory T cells.

article.title: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory.
article.abstract: NA: Obesity, which is often associated with prolonged exposure to an obesogenic diet, substantially alters immunity1-7, but whether brief dietary changes shape acute inflammatory responses and long-term tissue memory remains unclear. Here we show that transient high-fat diet (HFD) exposure at the onset of acute type 17 skin inflammation exacerbates disease in lean mice to levels comparable to those associated with chronic obesity. This effect is restricted to a discrete 4-day peri-initiation window; HFD outside this window has no impact, whereas switching obese mice to a low-fat diet (LFD) during a similar window fully blunts disease amplification. Mechanistically, HFD rapidly recruits neutrophils into the skin, and neutrophils in challenged skin express high levels of Nlrp3 (ref. 8) and Il1b. Neutrophil depletion, genetic Nlrp3 deficiency and pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition each blunt the HFD-induced inflammatory amplification. These findings nominate a neutrophil-NLRP3-IL-1β axis that licences pathogenic IL-1R1+CD4+ T helper type 17 (TH17) cells9,10. After recovery, a chromatin-poised tissue-resident memory T cell population persists. Consequently, mice exposed to HFD at disease onset develop exaggerated inflammation upon recurrence, despite recovery and maintenance on LFD. Transient HFD similarly amplifies lung TH17 inflammation through neutrophil- and IL-1R1-dependent mechanisms. Together, these findings show that dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory, suggesting that short-lived physiological states may become embedded in local immune memory11 when they coincide with tissue inflammation.

parsed.summary: This study investigates whether transient dietary changes during acute inflammation influence long-term tissue immune memory. Using lean mice with acute type 17 skin inflammation, researchers found that a 4-day high-fat diet (HFD) exposure at disease onset exacerbates inflammation comparably to chronic obesity. The effect is confined to a specific 4-day window; HFD outside this window has no impact. Switching obese mice to low-fat diet during the same window reduces disease severity. Mechanistically, HFD rapidly recruits neutrophils, which express Nlrp3 and Il1b, driving pathogenic TH17 cell activation. Neutrophil depletion, Nlrp3 deficiency, or NLRP3 inhibition mitigates inflammation. Post-recovery, a chromatin-poised tissue-resident memory T cell population persists, causing exaggerated inflammation upon recurrence despite subsequent LFD. The findings demonstrate that dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory through neutrophil-NLRP3-IL-1β axis activation.
key_findings: Transient high-fat diet exposure at disease onset exacerbates acute type 17 skin inflammation in lean mice
The inflammatory effect is restricted to a 4-day peri-initiation window; HFD outside this window has no impact
Neutrophil-mediated NLRP3-IL-1β axis drives pathogenic TH17 cell activation, with post-recovery tissue-resident memory T cells persisting
parsed.scientific_significance: This work establishes that short-lived dietary states during acute inflammation can durably reprogram tissue immune memory via neutrophil-NLRP3-IL-1β signaling, revealing a critical temporal window for dietary interventions to influence inflammatory disease trajectories.

article.title: Spin-Selective Hydrogen Utilization Enables Efficient Electrochemical CO2-to-CH4 Conversion in Ag-Modified Chiral Cu Catalysts for Unassisted Solar Fuel Production.
article.abstract: NA: Although electrochemical CO2-to-CH4 conversion offers a viable pathway to sustainable fuel synthesis, its efficiency is limited by the difficulty of balancing the availability of reactive hydrogen species for multistep CO2 hydrogenation against the suppression of the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, we establish a spin-selective catalytic strategy using Ag-modified chiral Cu electrocatalysts to overcome this intrinsic trade-off. Structural chirality in the Cu framework induces chirality-induced spin selectivity, which disfavors spin-singlet H2 formation, thereby mitigating the HER and favoring productive hydrogen utilization toward CO2 hydrogenation. Ag modification facilitates the supply of *CO intermediates on adjacent Cu sites. Thus, the chiral Ag/Cu catalyst selectively drives CO2 reduction toward CH4, delivering a CH4 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 67.0% at -0.7 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode while suppressing the HER. When coupled with perovskite-based photoelectrochemical electrodes, the chiral catalyst enables unassisted solar-driven CO2-to-CH4 conversion with an FECH4 of 54.1% and a solar-to-fuel efficiency of 5.86%. These results suggest spin-selective hydrogen utilization as an effective approach to selective hydrocarbon synthesis and bias-free solar CO2-to-fuel conversion.

parsed.summary: This study investigates spin-selective hydrogen utilization in Ag-modified chiral Cu electrocatalysts for efficient CO2-to-CH4 conversion. The researchers leveraged structural chirality to induce chirality-induced spin selectivity, which suppresses spin-singlet H2 formation and mitigates the competing hydrogen evolution reaction. Ag modification enhanced *CO intermediate supply, enabling a 67.0% CH4 Farada. The catalyst achieved unassisted solar-driven CO2-to-CH4 conversion with 54.1% CH4 FE and 5.86% solar-to-fuel efficiency.
key_findings: Chiral Cu frameworks with Ag modification suppress HER by favoring spin-selective hydrogen utilization
The catalyst achieves 67.0% CH4 Faradaic efficiency at -0.7 V vs. RHE
Unassisted solar-driven CO2-to-CH4 conversion yields 54.1% CH4 FE and 5.86% solar-to-fuel efficiency
parsed.scientific_significance: This work demonstrates spin-selective hydrogen utilization as a viable strategy for selective hydrocarbon synthesis and bias-free solar CO2-to-fuel conversion.

article.title: Causal associations between immune cell traits and hip osteoarthritis: A bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
article.abstract: NA: Observational studies have reported associations between immune cell phenotypes and hip osteoarthritis (HOA), but whether these associations are causal is unknown. We, therefore, used bidirectional 2-sample mendelian randomization (MR) to examine potential causal associations between 731 immune cell traits and HOA risk. Genome-Wide Association Study summary data for 731 immune cell traits were obtained from the genome-wide association study catalog, and HOA summary data were derived from the FinnGen Consortium. Instrumental variables were selected using significance thresholds of P < 1 × 10-5 for immune traits and P < 5 × 10-8 for HOA. The primary analysis used inverse variance weighted (IVW) MR, complemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, and simple mode methods. Sensitivity analyses included Cochran Q test, MR-Egger intercept test, mendelian randomization pleiotropy residual sum and outlier test, and leave-one-out analysis. False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction was applied to account for multiple testing. In the forward MR analysis, IVW identified 17 immune traits with FDR-significant associations with HOA risk (FDR < 0.05). Six CD33-expressing myeloid cell traits showed positive associations with HOA risk (odds ratio = 1.02, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.03 for all), while eleven immune traits including T cell, B cell, Natural Killer cell, regulatory T cell , and conventional dendritic cell phenotypes showed inverse associations (odds ratio range: 0.90-0.97), suggesting a potential protective role. Sensitivity analyses did not detect significant heterogeneity or horizontal pleiotropy for any of these 17 associations (all MR-Egger intercept P > .05; all Cochran's Q P > .05). Weighted median estimates were directionally concordant with IVW for all 17 traits, and every association met the prespecified cross-method consistency criterion (at least three of 5 methods directionally concordant). In the reverse MR analysis, 19 immune traits showed nominal associations (P < .05); however, none survived FDR correction (FDR > 0.05), providing no robust evidence for causal effects of HOA on immune cell composition. This MR study provides genetic evidence linking CD33-related myeloid traits and multiple lymphoid and monocyte phenotypes to HOA risk. These associations are statistical and do not establish biological mechanisms. Future experimental and clinical studies are needed to determine whether these immune phenotypes contribute to HOA pathophysiology.

parsed.summary: This study used bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization to investigate causal relationships between 731 immune cell traits and hip osteoarthritis (HOA) risk. Analysis identified 17 immune traits with statistically significant associations (FDR < 0.05) in the forward direction, including six CD33-expressing myeloid traits positively associated with HOA risk and eleven lymphoid/monocyte traits inversely associated. Reverse analysis showed no robust evidence for HOA causing immune changes. Findings suggest potential immune-mediated HOA mechanisms but require experimental validation.
key_findings: Six CD33-expressing myeloid cell traits showed positive associations with HOA risk (odds ratio 1.02, 95% CI 1.01-1.03)
Eleven immune traits including T cells, B cells, NK cells, regulatory T cells, and dendritic cells showed inverse associations with HOA risk (odds ratio range 0.90-0.97)
Reverse MR analysis found no robust evidence for causal effects of HOA on immune cell composition after FDR correction
parsed.scientific_significance: This study provides genetic evidence for immune cell traits influencing hip osteoarthritis risk through Mendelian randomization, advancing understanding of potential immunological pathways in osteoarthritis pathophysiology.

article.title: Atomic-Scale Design, Performance Degradation Mechanisms, and System Integration of Multi-Principal Element Hydrogen Storage Materials.
article.abstract: NA: Solid-state metal hydrides offer high volumetric hydrogen density and intrinsic safety for hydrogen storage, yet their practical application is severely hindered by poor room-temperature thermodynamics, sluggish kinetics, impurity gas poisoning, difficult activation, and cycling degradation. Multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) have recently emerged as promising candidates to overcome these bottlenecks through their vast compositional space, severe lattice distortion, and synergistic cocktail effect. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in MPEAs for solid-state hydrogen storage, bridging atomic-scale design to system-level performance. A unified composition-process-structure-property framework is established that integrates engineering-driven design rules, post-processing techniques, multi-scale computations, machine learning (ML), and high-throughput experiments. Using advanced in situ and ex situ characterization, the atomic-scale origins and cross-scale evolution of surface poisoning, hydrogen-induced amorphization (HIA), disproportionation, pulverization, and defect accumulation. A theoretical framework linking electronic structure to heat and mass transport is further developed, and hydrogen storage bed design, device integration, fuel-cell coupling, manufacturing scalability, and cost analysis are discussed. Finally, key scientific and engineering challenges and future research directions are outlined. This review provides scientific guidance for designing MPEA-based solid-state hydrogen storage systems with high capacity, long cycle life, high poisoning tolerance, fast de-/hydrogenation kinetics, and low cost.

parsed.summary: This review investigates multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) for solid-state hydrogen storage, addressing challenges like poor thermodynamics, slow kinetics, and degradation. It establishes a composition-process-structure-property framework integrating computational modeling, machine learning, and experimental techniques to understand atomic-scale degradation mechanisms such as hydrogen-induced amorphization and surface poisoning. The study identifies design principles for high-capacity, durable systems with fast kinetics and low cost, offering pathways for scalable hydrogen storage applications.
key_findings: MPEAs overcome hydrogen storage bottleneuses through atomic-scale design and synergistic effects
Advanced characterization reveals mechanisms of hydrogen-induced amorphization and surface poisoning
A unified framework links electronic structure to heat/mass transport for system-level optimization
parsed.scientific_significance: This work provides a foundational framework for designing robust, high-capacity solid-state hydrogen storage systems by elucidating atomic-scale degradation mechanisms and enabling multi-scale optimization strategies.

article.title: Oral Bacillus subtilis attenuates house dust mite-induced atopic dermatitis and is associated with altered mucosal immune responses.
article.abstract: NA: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease often presenting in infancy and increases the risk of developing other atopic disorders including food allergy, allergic rhinitis, and asthma. The rising prevalence of allergic diseases correlates with increasingly sterile living environments and reduced exposure to bacteria. This study hypothesized that exposure to nonpathogenic bacteria could help educate the immune system toward tolerance to innocuous allergens. Oral delivery of the probiotic bacterium Bacillus subtilis was used in a murine model of house dust mite (HDM)-induced AD. Oral administration of B. subtilis significantly reduced clinical symptoms of HDM-induced AD at weeks 3 and 7. B. subtilis treatment also reduced mast cell numbers in the skin at week 7 and showed a trend toward reducing epidermal thickness at week 3, although this was not statistically significant and was lost by week 7. While B. subtilis did not significantly reduce HDM-specific or total IgE or IgG1 levels, it increased levels of total IgA. The study found no significant changes in regulatory T cell numbers in the skin-draining lymph nodes. However, Treg numbers in the small intestine statistically increased 1 week after B. subtilis treatment. These findings support the role of probiotic treatment with B. subtilis as a tool to reduce the development and clinical symptoms of AD, associated with reduced mast cell accumulation, increased IgA levels, and increased intestinal regulatory T cell frequencies.

parsed.summary: This study investigated whether oral Bacillus subtilis could mitigate house dust mite-induced atopic dermatitis in mice. Using a murine model, the researchers administered B. subtilis and observed significant reductions in clinical symptoms at weeks 3 and 7. The probiotic also decreased skin mast cell counts and increased serum IgA levels, though effects on epidermal thickness were transient. No significant changes in HDM-specific IgE or regulatory T cells in lymph nodes were noted, but intestinal Treg frequencies rose post-treatment.
key_findings: Oral B. subtilis reduced clinical symptoms of house dust mite-induced atopic dermatitis in mice by weeks 3 and 7
B. subtilis decreased skin mast cell numbers and increased serum IgA levels
Intestinal regulatory T cell frequencies increased one week after treatment, though skin-draining lymph node Tregs remained unchanged
parsed.scientific_significance: This work demonstrates that oral probiotic administration can modulate mucosal immunity and reduce atopic dermatitis severity through mechanisms involving intestinal regulatory T cells and IgA elevation, offering insights into bacterial tolerance induction in allergic diseases.

article.title: Coupling Iodine Conversion and Zinc Ion Transport via Molecular Catalysis for Long-Life Zinc-Iodine Batteries.
article.abstract: NA: Zinc-iodine (Zn-I2) batteries are attractive for low-cost and scalable energy storage owing to their rapid iodine redox and high theoretical capacity. However, their practical application is severely limited by polyiodide shuttling and interfacial mass-transport imbalance, where polyiodide immobilization and Zn2+ accessibility are difficult to reconcile for continuous redox compensation, especially under high-rate conditions. Here, we address this adsorption-transport conflict by screening a series of metalated tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl) porphyrin molecular catalysts and identifying iron (III) meso-tetrakis (4-carboxyphenyl) porphyrin (Fe-TCPP) as a unified interfacial regulator catalyst. The Fe-N4 center provides moderate polyiodide binding, thereby stabilizing iodide intermediates without inducing interfacial passivation. Meanwhile, peripheral carboxyphenyl groups create a zincophilic microenvironment that promotes Zn2+ accessibility and local ion compensation. This coordinated regulation synchronizes electron transfer and ion redistribution, thereby sustaining reversible iodine redox while avoiding transport blockage. As a result, the Fe-TCPP-regulated iodine cathode delivers a specific capacity of 178 mAh g-1 and sustains 50 000 cycles at 5 A g-1. Moreover, a pouch cell with a high iodine loading of 22 mg cm-2 operates stably for more than 1300 cycles. This work establishes a molecular-catalytic framework for the simultaneous regulation of redox-intermediate adsorption-conversion and ionic transport in aqueous batteries involving soluble redox species.

parsed.summary: This study investigates enhancing zinc-iodine battery performance by resolving polyiodide shuttling and interfacial mass-transport issues. Using molecular catalyst screening, iron(III) meso-tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl) porphyrin (Fe-TCPP) was identified as an interfacial regulator that stabilizes iodide intermediates without passivating the interface and promotes zinc ion accessibility. The Fe-TCPP-regulated cathode achieves 178 mAh g-1 capacity and 50,000 cycles at 5 A g-1, demonstrating effective synchronization of electron transfer and ion redistribution for long-term stability.
key_findings: Fe-TCPP stabilizes iodide intermediates without interfacial passivation
Peripheral carboxyphenyl groups enhance zinc ion accessibility
The cathode achieves 178 mAh g-1 capacity and 50,000 cycles at 5 A g-1
parsed.scientific_significance: This work establishes a molecular-catalytic strategy for simultaneously regulating redox-intermediate conversion and ion transport in aqueous zinc-iodine batteries, addressing a critical bottleneck for practical implementation.

article.title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses characterize an IGF2BP3-MMP7-associated pattern in extracellular matrix remodeling and Treg-associated immune suppression in pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
article.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAAD) is characterized by extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. As an important N6-methyladenosine (m6A) reader, insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 3 (IGF2BP3) has been implicated in tumor progression; however, its downstream regulatory network and potential role in immune microenvironment remodeling remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: Public datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed to identify prognostic IGF2BP3-related genes. Functional enrichment analysis, prognostic model construction, immune infiltration analysis, somatic mutation profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomic analysis, and CellChat-based cell-cell communication analysis were performed. In vitro experiments, including qRT-PCR, western blotting, wound healing, transwell, CCK-8, and RNA stability assays, were conducted to evaluate the cellular effects of IGF2BP3 silencing. Multiplex immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, an orthotopic syngeneic mouse model, drug sensitivity analysis, and molecular docking were further performed to explore immune microenvironment associations and potential therapeutic implications.
RESULTS: IGF2BP3 was significantly upregulated in PAAD and associated with poor prognosis. MMP1, MMP7, and ITGA2 were identified as candidate IGF2BP3-associated ECM-related genes. IGF2BP3 knockdown was associated with changes in the proliferation, migration, and invasion of Panc-1 cells and was accompanied by decreased stability of these transcripts. A prognostic signature consisting of IGF2BP3, MMP1, MMP7, and ITGA2 demonstrated consistent prognostic stratification across multiple independent cohorts. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses revealed predominant expression of these genes in epithelial cell populations and highlighted their potential association with PAAD-related cellular states and intercellular communication. Among the downstream targets, MMP7 emerged as a candidate downstream effector based on RNA stability assays, SHAP feature importance analysis, gene interaction network analysis, and single-cell expression profiling. Both IGF2BP3 and MMP7 were positively associated with regulatory T-cell (Treg) infiltration. Spatial transcriptomic analyses further demonstrated significant spatial correlations among IGF2BP3, MMP7, and Treg-enriched immune niches, while multiplex immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, and an orthotopic syngeneic mouse model supported their association with immunosuppressive microenvironment features. Drug sensitivity analysis computationally prioritized Trametinib as a candidate for further investigation in high-risk PAAD, while molecular docking suggested favorable predicted interactions between Trametinib and the four signature proteins.
CONCLUSIONS: IGF2BP3 was associated with PAAD progression, and its depletion was accompanied by reduced stability of ECM-associated transcripts and changes in the tumor immune microenvironment. Integrated bulk transcriptomic, single-cell transcriptomic, spatial transcriptomic, and experimental analyses identify MMP7 as a candidate downstream effector associated with IGF2BP3 and suggest that the IGF2BP3-MMP7-associated pattern is related to Treg-enriched immunosuppressive niches in PAAD. Furthermore, Trametinib was identified as a hypothesis-generating therapeutic candidate for further evaluation in high-risk PAAD.

parsed.summary: This study investigated the role of IGF2BP3 in pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAAD) by integrating multi-omics and experimental approaches. It identified IGF2BP3 as significantly upregulated in PAAD with poor prognosis, linked to MMP1, MMP7, and ITGA2 in ECM remodeling. IGF2BP3 knockdown reduced cell proliferation, migration, and invasion while decreasing transcript stability. The IGF2BP3-MMP7 axis correlated with regulatory T-cell infiltration and immunosuppressive niches, suggesting a mechanism for tumor immune evasion. Trametinib was highlighted as a potential therapeutic candidate for high-risk PAAD.
key_findings: IGF2BP3 is significantly upregulated in pancreatic adenocarcinoma and associated with poor prognosis
IGF2BP3 knockdown reduces proliferation, migration, and invasion of pancreatic cancer cells and decreases stability of ECM-related transcripts
The IGF2BP3-MMP7 axis correlates with regulatory T-cell infiltration and immunosuppressive microenvironments in PAAD
parsed.scientific_significance: This work establishes a mechanistic link between IGF2BP3-driven ECM remodeling and Treg-mediated immunosuppression in pancreatic adenocarcinoma, providing a potential targetable pathway for immunotherapy.

article.title: Engineering High-Performance Flexible Electronics Through Scalable Manufacturing: Interplay of Materials, Processing, and Morphology.
article.abstract: NA: Flexible electronics have garnered extensive attention in recent years considering their promising applications across diverse fields such as communications, energy, display, healthcare, and wearable devices. Unlike laboratory-scale fabrication and integration, the transition of flexible electronics toward commercial applications demands scalable manufacturing that ensures high performance, large-area reproducibility, high yield, and throughput. However, achieving scalable manufacturing while maintaining device performance remains challenging, as fabrication scale-up often induces variations in material assembly, morphology evolution, and device integration, which may compromise functional reliability achieved at the laboratory scale. Generally, current flexible electronic devices can be divided into two categories: planar-type and fiber-type devices, representing two complementary platforms for realizing large-scale and highly integrated systems. In this review, scalable fabrication strategies tailored for each category and the latest advances are systematically summarized. In particular, the interplay among material design, scalable processing, morphology evolution, and device integration is highlighted, with emphasis on strategies that preserve device performance during manufacturing scale-up. Representative planar-type and fiber-type flexible electronic systems are further discussed to demonstrate how the synergistic optimization of material design and scalable manufacturing approaches enables high-performance devices for diverse applications. Finally, we outline remaining challenges and future directions to inform future developments in scalable flexible electronics.

parsed.summary: This review examines scalable manufacturing challenges in flexible electronics, focusing on maintaining high performance during scale-up. It analyzes the interplay between material design, processing techniques, morphology evolution, and device integration for both planar and fiber-type systems. The study highlights strategies that preserve functional reliability while enabling large-area reproducibility, high yield, and throughput in commercial applications.
key_findings: Scalable fabrication strategies maintain device performance during manufacturing scale-up
Material design and processing techniques must synergistically optimize morphology evolution
Planar and fiber-type flexible electronics require tailored approaches to ensure high-reproducibility systems
parsed.scientific_significance: This work provides a systematic framework for understanding how material selection and processing parameters interact to sustain high-performance flexible electronics during industrial-scale production.

article.title: Thioredoxin-1 induces immune tolerance against α-syn presented by MHC-II in microglia via promoting Tregs differentiation in MPTP-induced Parkinson's disease mice.
article.abstract: NA: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disease characterized by the loss of dopaminergic (DAergic) neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) and the formation of Lewy bodies composed of misfolded alpha-synuclein (α-syn). A growing number of studies indicate that microglia-mediated neuroinflammation and autoimmune responses are important pathological features of PD. Thioredoxin-1 (Trx-1), a multifunctional redox-regulatory protein, exerts neuroprotective effects in 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP)-induced PD models, but its impact on microglia-mediated autoimmune responses in PD remains unexplored. In the present study, we demonstrated that Trx-1 suppressed microglial accumulation and the increase of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Furthermore, Trx-1 suppressed the increase of α-syn and major histocompatibility complex class II (MHC-II)-mediated antigen presentation in microglia induced by MPTP. Additionally, MPTP promoted T helper 17 (Th17) cell differentiation, inhibited forkhead box P3 (FOXP3) protein level and regulatory T (Treg) cell differentiation, and enhanced forkhead box O1 (FOXO1) phosphorylation and nuclear exclusion in the SNpc. All these pathological alterations induced by MPTP were effectively restored by Trx-1 overexpression. Our findings highlight the pivotal role of Trx-1 in microglia-mediated autoimmune responses, thereby providing a potential therapeutic target for PD.

parsed.summary: This study investigated thioredoxin-1 (Trx-1) in MPTP-induced Parkinson's disease mice, focusing on its role in microglial immune responses. Trx-1 overexpression reduced microglial activation, pro-inflammatory cytokines, α-synuclein accumulation, and MHC-II-mediated antigen presentation. It also reversed MPTP-induced Th17 differentiation, FOXP3 suppression, and FOXO1 nuclear exclusion in the substantia nigra. These effects suggest Trx-1 promotes regulatory T cell differentiation to induce immune tolerance against α-synuclein presented by MHC-II in microglia, offering a potential neuroprotective mechanism for Parkinson's disease.
key_findings: Trx-1 overexpression suppressed MPTP-induced microglial activation and pro-inflammatory cytokine production
Trx-1 reduced α-synuclein accumulation and MHC-II-mediated antigen presentation in microglia
Trx-1 reversed MPTP-induced Th17 differentiation, FOXP3 suppression, and FOXO1 nuclear exclusion in the substantia nigra
parsed.scientific_significance: This study identifies thioredoxin-1 as a key regulator of microglial autoimmune responses in Parkinson's disease, providing mechanistic insight into how redox signaling can modulate neuroinflammation and immune tolerance.

article.title: Quantum Saturation of the Electro-Optic Effect.
article.abstract: NA: Future quantum computing architectures require electro-optic materials that maintain a strong, stable performance at cryogenic temperatures. In conventional electro-optic materials, large electro-optic coefficients are often confined to narrow temperature windows near structural phase transitions, where small changes in temperature lead to large changes in the electro-optic response. Using thermodynamic analysis, phase-field simulations, experimental growth, and cryogenic optical measurements, we show that quantum fluctuations can be harnessed to overcome this trade-off. By tuning the ferroelectric phase boundaries down to 0 K, quantum fluctuations induce a saturation regime in which a large electro-optic response becomes nearly temperature-independent below 25 K. We demonstrate that the phase boundaries can be tuned through either strain in BaTiO3 or through chemical composition in Ba1- xCaxTiO3, leading to a large, temperature-insensitive, cryogenic electro-optic response, reff =  2850 pm V-1 (experiment) and r51 =  2900 pm V-1 (theory) for BaTiO3 on GdScO3 and r51 =  1898 pm V-1 (theory) for Ba0.77Ca0.23TiO3. These values exceed the room temperature performance of bulk BaTiO3 r51 =  1600 pm V-1 and surpass the cryogenic performance of BaTiO3-on-Si, reff =  200 pm V-1, by over an order of magnitude. These findings establish a general design principle for engineering high-performance electro-optic materials for cryogenic applications.

parsed.summary: This study investigates quantum effects in electro-optic materials at cryogenic temperatures. By combining thermodynamic analysis, phase-field simulations, experimental growth, and cryogenic optical measurements, researchers demonstrated that quantum fluctuations can stabilize a large electro-optic response (reff = 2850 pm/V) near 0 K. The approach tuned ferroelectric phase boundaries to achieve temperature independence below 25 K, outperforming room-temperature and cryogenic benchmarks by orders of magnitude.
key_findings: Quantum fluctuations enable temperature-independent electro-optic response below 25 K
BaTiO3 on GdScO3 achieves reff = 2850 pm/V at cryogenic temperatures
Ba0.77Ca0.23TiO3 shows r51 = 1898 pm/V, surpassing BaTiO3-on-Si by over an order of magnitude
parsed.scientific_significance: This work establishes a quantum design principle for cryogenic electro-optic materials, overcoming traditional temperature sensitivity limitations through engineered phase boundaries.

article.title: Oncolytic Viruses Armed with Multiple Immunomodulatory Transgenes in Cancer Immunotherapy.
article.abstract: NA: Oncolytic viruses (OVs) have emerged as versatile cancer immunotherapeutic agents that selectively kill tumor cells while simultaneously inducing antitumor immune responses. The therapeutic activity of OVs can be further enhanced by arming them with immunomodulatory transgenes. However, expression of a single transgene often fails to generate durable antitumor immunity, largely because of the complex, immunosuppressive nature of the tumor microenvironment (TME). To overcome this limitation, recent advances in OV engineering have focused on co-expression of multiple immunomodulatory payloads, including a combination of cytokines, cytokine receptors, costimulatory molecules, chemokines, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), bispecific T-cell engagers, viral antigens, and tumor antigens. Increasing evidence indicates that multi-transgene-armed OVs can more effectively promote dendritic cell maturation, enhance intratumoral infiltration and activation of CD8+ T cells and natural killer cells, elevate effector-to-regulatory T-cell ratios, remodel immunosuppressive TMEs, and synergize with other immunotherapies, including ICI and adoptive cell therapy. Despite growing interest in this field, a comprehensive review focused specifically on the immunological mechanisms, therapeutic efficacy, and translational challenges of multi-transgene-expressing OVs remains lacking. In this review, we summarize multi-transgene-armed OVs, highlighting the mechanistic rationale underlying transgene combinations, outlining their antitumor effects across preclinical settings, and discussing key design principles for next-generation OV-based immunotherapies.

parsed.summary: This review examines multi-transgene-armed oncolytic viruses (OVs) for cancer immunotherapy. It addresses how co-expressing multiple immunomodulatory transgenes—such as cytokines, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and T-cell activators—overcomes limitations of single-transgene OVs by enhancing dendritic cell maturation, CD8+ T cell infiltration, and TME remodeling. The study emphasizes their potential to improve antitumor immunity and synergize with existing immunotherapies in preclinical models.
key_findings: Co-expression of multiple immunomodulatory transgenes enhances dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell infiltration in tumors
Multi-transgene OVs remodel immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments and improve effector-to-regulatory T cell ratios
These Ousing OVs synergize with immune checkpoint inhibitors and adoptive cell therapies in preclinical settings
parsed.scientific_significance: This review establishes multi-transgene-armed oncolytic viruses as a promising strategy to overcome tumor immunosuppression through coordinated immune activation, advancing the design of next-generation cancer immunotherapies.

article.title: Bismuth-Mediated Zinc Extraction-Induced Carbon Defects Boost Fe Single-Atom Catalysis for Efficient Oxygen Reduction.
article.abstract: NA: Fe single-atom catalysts with Fe-N4 configurations typically suffer from excessive adsorption of oxygenated intermediates, leading to intrinsic limitations in catalytic efficiency. Here, we propose a Bi-mediated Fe-adjacent Zn extraction strategy to create defects adjacent to Fe-N4 moieties on ZIF-8-derived carbon support, thereby tailoring the local microenvironment of Fe single atoms. The resulting Fe-N-pCd catalyst exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity in alkaline electrolyte, delivering a half-wave potential of 0.918 V versus RHE along with excellent durability. The assembled quasi-solid-state Zn-air battery using Fe-N-pCd as the air cathode catalyst affords stable operation for over 3000 h at -40°C. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that the formed carbon defects adjacent to Fe-N4 sites redistribute the local electron density and favor the formation of an axial *OH-bound Fe state under ORR conditions. This defect-modulated coordination environment lowers the Fe d-band center and alleviates the overly strong Fe-*OH coupling, thereby changing the potential-limiting step from *OH removal to *OOH formation and accelerating ORR kinetics. This study provides a neighboring-template extraction route for engineering defect microenvironments adjacent to metal single atoms, opening new opportunities for the design of efficient ORR electrocatalysts.

parsed.summary: This study addresses the intrinsic inefficiency of Fe single-atom catalysts (Fe-N4) by engineering carbon defects adjacent to Fe sites using bismuth-mediated zinc extraction from ZIF-8. The Fe-N-pCd catalyst achieved a high half-wave potential of 0.918 V vs. RHE in alkaline electrolytes and demonstrated stable Zn-air battery operation beyond 3000 hours at -40°C. Defects redistributed electron density, favoring an axial *OH-bound Fe state and accelerating oxygen reduction kinetics by altering the rate-limiting step.
key_findings: Bismuth-mediated zinc extraction creates carbon defects adjacent to Fe-N4 sites on ZIF-8-derived carbon
Fe-N-pCd catalyst achieved 0.918 V half-wave potential vs. RHE in alkaline electrolytes
Quasi-solid-state Zn-air battery with Fe-N-pCd cathode operated stably for over 3000 hours at -40°C
parsed.scientific_significance: This work establishes a defect engineering strategy to optimize single-atom catalyst microenvironments, enhancing oxygen reduction kinetics by modifying electronic structure and reaction pathways.

article.title: Peripheral Blood Transcriptomic Candidates Associated With Pseudoexfoliation Syndrome and Pseudoexfoliation Glaucoma: A Bioinformatics Analysis.
article.abstract: NA: The molecular mechanism of pseudoexfoliation glaucoma (PXG) is still unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate biomarkers of PXG, with the goal of providing a theoretical basis. Ten blood samples from patients with pseudoexfoliation syndrome (PEX), 10 blood samples from PXG patients, and 10 control blood samples were collected for transcriptome sequencing. A total of three candidate biomarkers (ACTA2, IL1RN, and MMP9) were identified. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that the three candidate biomarkers were involved in the regulation of the actin cytoskeleton and the leukocyte transendothelial migration pathway. The results of the peripheral immune cell proportion analysis suggested altered peripheral immune profiles among the three groups, involving memory B-cells, CD8+ T-cells, regulatory T-cells, M0 macrophages, and resting CD4+ memory T-cells. Correlation analysis further revealed associations between the candidate biomarkers and these differential immune cell subsets. Exploratory drug‒gene interaction analysis provided preliminary insights for future therapeutic investigations. In an RT-qPCR validation set consisting of 15 peripheral whole blood samples (5 PEX, 5 PXG, and 5 control samples), the mRNA expression levels of the candidate biomarkers were assessed across the three groups. RT-qPCR validation revealed that ACTA2 and MMP9 were significantly upregulated in PXG patients compared with controls, whereas ACTA2, MMP9, and IL1RN were elevated in PEX patients compared with both controls and PXG patients. Collectively, these findings suggest that the three candidate biomarkers may be associated with PEX/PXG-related molecular alterations.

parsed.summary: This study investigated transcriptomic differences between pseudoexfoliation syndrome (PEX), pseudoex. glaucoma (PXG), and control blood samples to identify potential biomarkers. Using RNA-seq and validation via RT-qPCR, three candidate biomarkers (ACTA2, IL1RN, MMP9) were identified. These genes were associated with actin cytoskeleton regulation and leukocyte transendothelial migration pathways. The biomarkers showed differential expression across PEX and PXG groups, suggesting molecular alterations in pseudoexfoliation pathology.
key_findings: Three candidate biomarkers (ACTA2, IL1RN, MMP9) were identified through transcriptome sequencing of blood samples from PEX, PXG, and control groups.
Gene set enrichment analysis linked the biomarkers to actin cytoskeleton regulation and leukocyte transendothelial migration pathways.
RT-qPCR validation confirmed significant upregulation of ACTA2 and MMP9 in PXG patients versus controls, with elevated levels in PEX patients compared to both controls and PXG.
parsed.scientific_significance: The identification of these biomarkers provides potential molecular targets for understanding pseudoexfoliation glaucoma pathophysiology and may inform future therapeutic strategies.

article.title: Discovery of Small-Molecule Cryoprotectants Using Pretrained Language Model Representations.
article.abstract: NA: Cryopreservation supports cell therapy, transfusion medicine, and tissue banking, but cryoprotectant selection remains constrained by empirical screening, toxicity, and ice recrystallization. We used pretrained language models as SMILES sequence encoders to prioritize small-molecule cryoprotectants for experimental testing. Hierarchical representations were coupled to descriptor reconstruction, gated fusion, and downstream prediction of normalized mean grain size and thresholded labels. Splat-cooling measurements assessed candidate ice recrystallization inhibition, followed by compatibility and cryopreservation experiments in red blood cells, human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells and rat abdominal aortas. Selected additives improved recovery or preservation endpoints within the tested formulations. This representation-based screening workflow connects molecular property prediction with experimental cryobiology across ice, cellular, and tissue endpoints.

parsed.summary: This study addresses cryoprotectant selection challenges by leveraging pretrained language models to encode small-molecule structures as SMILES sequences. The approach prioritized candidates through hierarchical representations, descriptor reconstruction, and prediction of ice recrystallization metrics. Experimental validation in red blood cells, stem cells, and tissues showed improved cryopreservation outcomes with selected additives, demonstrating a computational screening method linking molecular properties to functional cryobiological endpoints.
key_findings: Pretrained language models encoded small-molecule structures to prioritize cryoprotectant candidates
Predicted ice recrystusing normalized mean grain size and thresholded labels
Selected additives enhanced cryopreservation recovery in red blood cells, stem cells, and tissues
parsed.scientific_significance: This work establishes a computational framework for predicting cryoprotectant efficacy across multiple biological scales, bridging molecular property prediction with experimental cryobiology outcomes.

article.title: Immune cell mediated fibrosis after kidney transplantation: mechanisms and emerging immunomodulatory therapies.
article.abstract: NA: Renal allograft fibrosis is a common histological endpoint after multiple injuries, rather than an independent disease entity. Despite modern immunosuppression, recurrent alloimmune injury, ischemia reperfusion injury, infection, donor and recipient related factors, and drug toxicity can converge on interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy. This review examines how innate and adaptive immune responses contribute to the transition from early graft injury to chronic remodeling, with particular emphasis on cellular plasticity and intercellular communication. Human single cell and spatial studies show that immune, tubular epithelial, endothelial, and stromal cells form heterogeneous, stage dependent networks rather than fixed pathogenic populations. We prioritize evidence from human kidney allografts while clearly identifying mechanisms inferred from experimental models. Established immunosuppression remains essential for preventing immune mediated graft injury, whereas regulatory T cell therapies, macrophage state modulation, cytokine blockade, and CD38 directed therapy remain investigational. None has been proven to reverse established allograft fibrosis. Future diagnosis and treatment should integrate Banff histology, donor specific antibodies, donor derived cell free DNA, urinary chemokines, and biopsy-based transcriptomics. Clinical trials should determine whether targeted immunomodulation can slow the progression of allograft fibrosis and preserve long-term graft function and survival.
article.journal_name: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

parsed.summary: This review investigates the mechanisms driving renal allograft fibrosis post-transplantation, focusing on immune cell contributions. It analyzes how innate and adaptive immune responses transition injury to chronic remodeling, emphasizing cellular plasticity and communication. Human studies reveal dynamic networks of immune and stromal cells rather than static pathogenic populations. Current immunosuppression prevents injury, but emerging therapies like regulatory T cell modulation and cytokine blockade remain investigational without proven efficacy against established fibrosis.
key_findings: Renal allograft fibrosis results from multiple injury pathways converging on interstitial fibrosis and tubular atusing
Human single-cell and spatial analyses indicate heterogeneous, stage-dependent immune-stromal networks rather than fixed pathogenic cell populations
Emerging immunomodulatory therapies lack proven efficacy in reversing established allograft fibrosis
parsed.scientific_significance: This work clarifies the dynamic immune-stromal interactions in renal allograft fibrosis, providing a foundation for targeted interventions to prevent progression while highlighting the need for integrated diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

article.title: High-Density Pixelated Metasurfaces for Terahertz Hyperspectral Imaging.
article.abstract: NA: Metasurface-enabled terahertz imaging and spectroscopy are moving toward compact, high-throughput systems, but current approaches remain limited by discrete spectral sampling, computational reconstruction, and the trade-off between spatial resolution and resonance quality in nonlocal designs. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different paradigm based on photonic crystal heterojunction-enabled pixelated metasurfaces that directly encode spatial information into spectrally resolved, high-quality-factor resonances. By embedding bound-state-in-the-continuum metapixels within a bandgap-engineered heterostructure, we simultaneously suppress lateral leakage and control vertical radiation, enabling effective three-dimensional photon confinement in finite metasurfaces. This mechanism overcomes the conventional dependence of resonance quality on pixel size, yielding enhanced quality factors and figure of merit without increasing the device footprint, and enabling metapixels with lateral dimensions of ∼2λ that retain high spectral fidelity and signal-to-noise ratio. Leveraging this capability, we realize a 3 × 3 pixelated metasurface supporting nine independently addressable resonances, all retrieved in a single-shot broadband terahertz measurement. The resulting spectral-spatial encoding strategy establishes a direct one-to-one mapping between resonance signatures and spatial pixels, enabling hyperspectral imaging with a single-pixel detector and a THz pulse, without raster scanning or algorithmic inversion. These results provide a scalable route toward real-time terahertz imaging and integrated photonic sensing.

parsed.summary: This study investigates enhancing terahertz hyperspectral imaging using high-density pixelated metasurfaces. The approach leverages photonic crystal heterojunctions to create pixelated metasurfaces that encode spatial information into spectrally resolved resonances. Key results include suppressing lateral leakage, enabling three-dimensional photon confinement, and achieving nine independently addressable resonances in a single 3×3 pixel array. The system operates with a single-pixel detector and THz pulse, eliminating raster scanning and computational reconstruction.
key_findings: Pixelated metasurfaces with ∼2λ lateral dimensions retain high spectral fidelity and signal-to-noise ratio
Three-dimensional photon confinement enables enhanced quality factors without increasing device footprint
Single-shot broadband terahertz measurement retrieves nine independently addressable resonances
parsed.scientific_significance: This work establishes a direct spectral-spatial encoding mechanism for terahertz hyperspectral imaging, overcoming traditional limitations in spatial resolution, spectral sampling, and computational requirements.

article.title: Mechanisms and Implications of SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Hematopoietic System.
article.abstract: NA: COVID-19 disrupts hematopoiesis across the entire hierarchy, from hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) to mature blood cells. Several hematological abnormalities-lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia and elevated D-dimer-are consistently associated with disease severity and mortality. Within the HSPC compartment, ACE2 and TMPRSS2 expression is largely restricted to rare CD133 + CD34+Lin-CD45 - precursors, suggesting that hematopoietic injury may arise substantially from non-infectious exposure to spike protein and inflammatory mediators rather than from direct viral infection. Downstream events include NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis, virus-induced senescence with a senescence-associated secretory phenotype, epigenetic reprogramming, and skewed lineage output. These cell-intrinsic changes are compounded by remodeling of the bone marrow niche by stromal, endothelial, and osteoblastic cells. Clinically, these changes manifest as lymphopenia with T-cell exhaustion and disturbed regulatory T-cell balance, thrombocytopenia due to impaired megakaryopoiesis and immune-mediated clearance, coagulopathy involving neutrophil extracellular trap formation and endothelial injury, and anemia reflecting disordered iron handling and red-cell damage. These abnormalities can persist in a subset of patients long after viral clearance. These mechanistic insights inform current management, including antiviral therapy for prolonged viral shedding, corticosteroids for severe disease, severity-stratified anticoagulation, and supportive measures to promote marrow recovery. The hematological implications of vaccination are also considered: although rare immune thrombotic events have been reported, their mechanism appears distinct from spike-protein-induced injury, and the overall benefit-risk balance of vaccination remains favorable. We distinguish conclusions supported by clinical data from those based on in vitro or observational evidence and highlight open questions for future research.

parsed.summary: This study investigates how SARS-CoV-2 infection disrupts hematopoiesis, focusing on hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) and mature blood cells. It identifies ACE2 and TMPRSS2 expression in rare HSPC precursors, suggesting injury may stem from spike protein and inflammatory mediators rather than direct viral infection. Key mechanisms include NLRP3 inflammasome activation, pyroptosis, senescence, epigenetic changes, and niche remodeling. These lead to lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, and anemia, which can persist post-viral clearance. The findings inform clinical management strategies and vaccination benefits.
key_findings: SARS-CoV-2 infection causes hematopoietic injury via non-infectious mechanisms involving spike protein and inflammatory mediators rather than direct viral infection in HSPCs
Mechanisms include NLRP3 inflammasome activation, pyroptosis, senescence, epigenetic reprogramming, and bone marrow niche remodeling
Hematological abnormalities such as lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, and anemia persist post-viral clearance in some patients
parsed.scientific_significance: This work elucidates the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying SARS-CoV-2-induced hematopoietic dysfunction, providing critical insights for understanding long-term hematological complications and guiding targeted therapeutic interventions.

article.title: Dynamic, Wet-Adhesive Hydrogels for Enhanced Interface Healing in Cartilage Repair.
article.abstract: NA: Articular cartilage defects remain a major clinical challenge due to the tissue's limited self-repair capacity. Although numerous biomaterial-based strategies have been explored, achieving a stable and functional cartilage interface remains difficult. A critical barrier is the poor integration between grafts and native cartilage, leading to fibrocartilage formation, delamination, and repair failure. Current approaches show limited success due to inadequate wet adhesion, mechanical mismatch, and insufficient chemical bonding. Here, we report a dynamically adaptive wet-adhesive hydrogel composed of oxidized hyaluronic acid, quaternized chitosan, and silk fibroin (OHA/QCS/SF) for enhanced cartilage interface healing. The precursor exhibited rapid underwater spreading on hydrated substrates and displaced interfacial fluid in a fluid-covered assay. Fluorescence imaging further revealed wetting and infiltration into the PAAm hydrogel. Dynamic Schiff-base bonding between aldehyde groups in the hydrogel and amine-containing components at the cartilage interface further promoted wet adhesion, while the reversible network enabled self-healing under mechanical disturbance. In a rabbit cartilage defect model, the hydrogel loaded with synovial membrane-derived mesenchymal stem cells (SMSCs) improved defect filling, host-graft integration, and cartilage-like regeneration. This study provides a dynamic wet-adhesive hydrogel strategy for improving biomaterial-cartilage interface healing in fluid-rich joint environments.

parsed.summary: Articular cartilage defects pose significant repair challenges due to limited self-repair capacity. This study developed a dynamically adaptive wet-adhesive hydrogel (OHA/QCS/SF) to enhance interface healing. The hydrogel demonstrated rapid underwater spreading, fluid displacement, and infiltration into cartilage interfaces. It promoted wet adhesion via dynamic Schiff-base bonding and self-healing under mechanical stress. In rabbit models, it improved defect filling, host-graft integration, and cartilage regeneration when loaded with synovial membrane-derived mesenchymal stem cells.
key_findings: The hydrogel exhibited rapid underwater spreading and fluid displacement at cartilage interfaces
Dynamic Schiff-base bonding enabled wet adhesion and self-healing under mechanical stress
In rabbit cartilage defects, the hydrogel with SMSCs enhanced defect filling and host-graft integration
parsed.scientific_significance: This work provides a dynamic wet-adhesive hydrogel strategy for improving biomaterial-cartilage interface healing in fluid-rich joint environments, addressing a critical barrier to effective cartilage repair.

article.title: CXCL16-CXCR6 axis drives the enrichment of CCR8+ effector regulatory T cells and shapes an immunosuppressive microenvironment in the colorectal cancer liver metastatic niche.
article.abstract: NA: The mechanisms underlying regulatory T cell (Treg) enrichment and immunosuppressive activity in colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell transcriptomic analysis with experimental and tissue-based validation to investigate Treg heterogeneity and its potential regulation in CRLM. Our findings revealed a shift toward effector Treg states in metastatic lesions, characterized by increased CCR8 expression and associated with an immunosuppressive landscape. CellChat analysis identified CXCL16-CXCR6 as a candidate signaling axis between myeloid or dendritic populations and effector Tregs. In vitro chemotaxis assays demonstrated preferential migration of CCR8+ Tregs toward CXCL16, and this response was attenuated by CXCR6 blockade. Analyses of human CRLM cohorts and tissue samples further linked CCR8+ effector Treg enrichment to reduced effector T-cell abundance and increased inhibitory-checkpoint expression. Collectively, these findings implicate CXCL16-CXCR6-mediated chemotaxis in the accumulation of effector Tregs with immunosuppressive features in CRLM and highlight CCR8 as a marker of these Treg states, providing insight into the interplay between CXCL16-expressing myeloid populations and Tregs in the metastatic liver microenvironment.

parsed.summary: This study investigated Treg heterogeneity in colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) using single-cell transcriptomics and experimental validation. It identified a shift toward CCR8+ effector Tregs with immunosuppressive traits, linked to CXCL16-CXCR6 signaling. In vitro assays showed CCR8+ Tregs migrate toward CXCL16, and CXCR6 blockade reduced this response. Human CRLM samples correlated CCR8+ Treg enrichment with reduced effector T cells and increased inhibitory checkpoints, suggesting CXCL16-CXCR6 drives immunosuppressive microenvironment formation in CRLM.
key_findings: CXCL16-CXCR6 signaling promotes CCR8+ effector Treg accumulation in colorectal cancer liver metastases
CCR8+ effector Tregs in CRLM show reduced effector T-cell abundance and elevated inhibitory checkpoint expression
CXCR6 blockade attenuates CXCL16-mediated chemotaxis of CCR8+ Tregs in vitro
parsed.scientific_significance: The study establishes CXCL16-CXCR6 as a key axis driving immunosuppressive Treg enrichment in colorectal cancer liver metastases, revealing a mechanism for metastatic niche immunosuppression.

article.title: Liquid Luminescent Materials Based on 10H-Pyrido[1,2-a]-5-indolium Salts.
article.abstract: NA: Next-generation flexible optoelectronics and soft robotics require adaptive luminescent materials that withstand extreme environments while remaining deformable. However, the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of current solvent-free ionic liquids suffers from fundamental limitations arising from aggregation-caused quenching and rapid nonradiative decay, and these liquids degrade under thermal and chemical stress. This study presents a supramolecular locking strategy that overcomes these limitations through kinetically stabilized anion-π+ interactions. Specifically, a rigid N-doped fluorene (10H-pyrido[1,2-a]-5-indolium, PIn+) was paired with selected anions to maintain fluidity and suppress nonradiative molecular motion by locking radiative pathways in the liquid state. This ionic tethering approach yielded an unprecedented PLQY of 80% in the liquid state while preserving the solvent-free liquid nature of the material. These highly emissive ionic liquids exhibited extreme physicochemical robustness, withstanding thermal decomposition up to 400°C, retaining intense emission without volatilization even under reduced pressure at 250°C, and resisting strongly acidic and basic environments. Derived from a versatile and readily synthesizable fluorene platform, this system also provides broad opportunities for structural customization. These findings establish a general molecular design principle for highly robust and emissive liquid fluorophores, providing a foundation for indestructible and flexible photonic technologies operating under extreme conditions.

parsed.summary: This study addresses the need for adaptive luminescent materials in extreme environments by developing solvent-free ionic liquids with enhanced photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Using supramolecular locking via anion-π+ interactions, researchers achieved 80% PLQ. The materials retained high emission under thermal stress (up to 400°C), vacuum (250°C), and acidic/basic conditions, demonstrating exceptional robustness while maintaining fluidity. This approach enables durable photonic applications in harsh conditions.
key_findings: 80% photoluminescence quantum yield in liquid state
Thermal stability up to 400°C
Resistance to acidic and basic environments without degradation
parsed.scientific_significance: This work establishes a molecular design strategy for highly robust, emissive liquid fluorophores that overcome aggregation-caused quenching and nonradiative decay, enabling photonic technologies in extreme environments.

article.title: Distinct Treg-Mediated Cardiac Remodeling in HFpEF Mice Treated With Neonatal Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Their Secretome.
article.abstract: NA: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction lacks effective disease-modifying therapies. We show that neonatal mesenchymal stem cells and their secretome improve diastolic function by expanding regulatory T cells, reducing inflammation and fibrosis. Our new causal machine learning framework, variable importance prediction for cellular function, identified causal immune pathways driving cardiac functional improvement and revealed regulatory T cells as a therapeutic target.

parsed.summary: This study investigated whether neonatal mesenchymal stem cells and their secretome could improve diastolic function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) mice. Using a causal machine learning framework, the researchers identified regulatory T cells as key mediators of cardiac remodeling. The treatment reduced inflammation and fibrosis while expanding regulatory T cells, leading to improved diastolic function in HFp. The findings suggest a potential therapeutic target for HFpEF.
key_findings: Neonatal mesenchymal stem cells and their secretome improved diastolic function in HFpEF mice
Regulatory T cells were expanded and mediated cardiac remodeling improvements
The treatment reduced inflammation and fibrosis in the heart
parsed.scientific_significance: This work identifies regulatory T cells as a causal mechanism for diastolic function improvement in HFpEF, providing a novel therapeutic target for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

article.title: Ion-Electron Coupling Transport in Semiconductor Nanotubes for Retinomorphic Vision.
article.abstract: NA: A key limitation of current artificial visual systems lies in their single-channel signal transduction, which fundamentally departs from the parallel processing architecture of the biological retinas enabled by rod and cone cells. To bridge this gap, we developed a retinomorphic vision device by ion-electron coupling transport based on carbon nanotube (CNT)/zinc oxide (ZnO) heterostructured nanotubes. Upon optical stimuli, this device generates two distinct ionic and electronic current signals, effectively mimicking the parallel phototransduction pathways in biological vision. This dual-channel property enables efficient machine vision perception, achieving luminance adaptation and color discrimination accuracies of 96.5% and 98.2%, respectively. Furthermore, traffic-light-guided closed-loop navigation of a mobile vehicle in a real scene has verified its application potential in embodied intelligence. This "single device enabled, distinguishable dual-channel readouts" principle opens a new avenue toward artificial vision systems.

parsed.summary: This study addresses the limitation of single-channel signal transduction in artificial vision systems by developing a retinomorphic device using carbon nanotube/zinc oxide heterostructured nanotubes. The device generates dual ionic and electronic signals upon optical stimulation, mimicking biological reticulate phototransduction. It achieves 96.5% luminance adaptation and 98.2% color discrimination accuracy, demonstrating potential for embodied intelligence applications through real-world navigation.
key_findings: The device produces distinct ionic and electronic current signals upon light exposure
It achieves 96.5% luminance adaptation and 98.2% color discrimination accuracy
Real-world traffic-light guided navigation validates its application in embodied intelligence
parsed.scientific_significance: This work establishes a dual-channel signal transduction mechanism in a single device that mimics biological retinal parallel processing, advancing artificial vision systems beyond conventional single-channel approaches.
